When an astronomer does observations with a telescope this happens during the night at that telescope. By the end of the summer the team had photographed sixty thousand pages and filled four notebooks with corrections, and the reading room smelled of dust, coffee and warm electronics. Visitors started coming on Saturdays, mostly people looking for birth records or property deeds, and a retired teacher spent her afternoons explaining the catalogue to them. The project ran out of money in October, as everyone had predicted, but the work continued at a slower pace through the winter, one box a week, with a single volunteer and a borrowed lamp. What remained at the end was not the building or the shelving but the list: a document that described, page by page, what the city had kept and what it had thrown away.
